findings.title: GET / depends on an undefined session-selection contract
findings.evidence: "The `TimelineViewModel` is populated at page-render time via `IDhfRepository.ListSessionsAsync` and `IDhfRepository.ListEntriesAsync` for the selected session."
findings.problem: The only documented route is `GET /`, but the spec never defines how the "selected session" is chosen, how a user switches sessions, or what happens when no session exists.
findings.why_it_matters: The mandatory page cannot be implemented deterministically, and tests cannot assert the correct entries without guessing hidden state or UI behavior.
findings.proposed_fix: Define the selection contract explicitly, e.g. `GET /?sessionId={uuid}` with default-to-latest behavior when absent, plus the empty-state behavior when there are no sessions.

findings.title: Entry detail JSON schema is unspecified
findings.evidence: "Full JSON detail including `ToolCallRow[]` and `DecorationRow[]`. Used by the entry detail page."
findings.problem: The response references `ToolCallRow[]` and `DecorationRow[]` but does not define any fields, types, nullability, ordering guarantees, or nested object shapes.
findings.why_it_matters: The entry-detail page and its tests cannot be built without inventing a private schema that will create integration churn.
findings.proposed_fix: Add the exact JSON contract for `/api/dhf/entries/{entryId}`, including every field name, type, enum domain, nullability, ordering, and screenshot URL/path representation.

findings.title: Integrity endpoint timeout behavior is not represented in its API contract
findings.evidence: Section 13: "The endpoint returns what's been validated so far with a truncation flag." Section 5.3 response example contains only `sessionId`, `mode`, `valid`, `entriesChecked`, `failures`, and `warnings`.
findings.problem: The spec mandates partial results on timeout but omits the `truncation` field and any fields needed to interpret partial validation safely.
findings.why_it_matters: Clients cannot distinguish a complete validation from a timed-out partial result, so the integrity indicator can misreport session health.
findings.proposed_fix: Extend the `/api/dhf/integrity` schema with explicit partial-result fields such as `truncated`, `timeoutMs`, and `lastSequenceChecked`, and define how `valid` must be interpreted when `truncated=true`.

findings.title: Repository-failure handling contradicts Postgres-unreachable handling
findings.evidence: "**IDhfRepository throws:** The endpoint returns 500..." and "**Postgres is unreachable:** ... The JSON endpoints return 503."
findings.problem: A Postgres outage will typically surface as an `IDhfRepository` exception, but the spec assigns both 500 and 503 to that condition without defining how implementations distinguish them.
findings.why_it_matters: Different handlers will produce inconsistent status codes and UI behavior for the same failure, breaking tests and observability.
findings.proposed_fix: Define an exception taxonomy or repository result contract, e.g. `RepositoryUnavailableException => 503`, all other repository exceptions => 500, and specify the page/banner behavior for each.

findings.title: Screenshot endpoint validates only filename, leaving addinSessionId as an unchecked path segment
findings.evidence: "Solution: a `GET /screenshots/{addinSessionId}/{filename}` endpoint that validates the filename... Path traversal guards: reject any filename containing `..`, `/`, `\`, or null bytes."
findings.problem: The path-traversal rules apply only to `filename`; `addinSessionId` is inserted into the filesystem path with no documented validation or canonical-path check.
findings.why_it_matters: A malicious or malformed `addinSessionId` can escape the screenshot root or target another session's files if path joining is implemented naively.
findings.proposed_fix: Constrain `addinSessionId` to a strict format (for example UUID), build the full path canonically, and reject any resolved path that is not under `ScreenshotRootPath`.

findings.title: Stretch-enabled startup is not cross-platform or deterministic as specified
findings.evidence: Section 10: "these tests can run on any OS with .NET 8." Section 12 config uses `"%LOCALAPPDATA%\\BSVoiceCAD\\screenshots"` and says "The viewer will throw at startup if `screenshotRootPath` doesn't exist (stretch endpoints only...)"
findings.problem: The spec relies on a Windows-style path placeholder without defining environment-variable expansion, while also claiming any-OS test execution and enabling stretch endpoints in the example config.
findings.why_it_matters: Linux/macOS CI or local test runs will fail at startup unless each environment invents its own path-resolution override behavior.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify path expansion behavior explicitly, provide a cross-platform default or mandatory test override, and document that stretch endpoints must be disabled by default when no valid screenshot root is configured.

findings.title: Read consistency is undefined while the orchestrator is actively appending entries
findings.evidence: The viewer runs "in-process with the orchestrator"; `GET /` uses separate `ListSessionsAsync` and `ListEntriesAsync` calls; `app.js` polls every 3 seconds; shallow/deep integrity validation reads live session data.
findings.problem: The spec does not define snapshot isolation, transaction boundaries, or behavior for validating/opening a session that is being written concurrently.
findings.why_it_matters: Counts, timelines, and hash-chain validation can become internally inconsistent or falsely report tampering when reads span concurrent writes.
findings.proposed_fix: Define repository read-isolation requirements for viewer endpoints, or explicitly restrict integrity validation and timeline counts to a stable snapshot/closed session.

findings.title: ACC-08 performance testing is not reproducible as an automated test
findings.evidence: "Must render within 1 second for a 20-entry session on the demo laptop (GE75)." and "`TimelinePerformanceTests` — ACC-08; 20-entry session renders within 1s on representative hardware (integration test)"
findings.problem: The acceptance threshold is tied to a specific machine class, but the required automated tests are otherwise described as portable and in-process.
findings.why_it_matters: CI results will be noisy or meaningless because the pass/fail condition depends on hardware, warmup, and host load that the spec does not control.
findings.proposed_fix: Move ACC-08 to a controlled benchmark/manual acceptance procedure, or define a reproducible performance harness with fixed environment, warmup, and measurement methodology.

top_3_must_fix: Define how `GET /` selects a session and what happens when no session exists.
Define read-isolation/snapshot behavior for timeline and integrity reads while sessions are still being written.
Fix the contradictory and incomplete API contracts around failure handling and integrity partial results.
